description: Fix broken streaming pipeline (clients see 'off air' during active stream) by making useAudioCapture a singleton, fixing public site polling/reconnection, fixing FlowStreaming status polling bugs, and adding an optional stream recording checkbox.

steps.task: Refactor useAudioCapture.ts to singleton pattern (like useStreamSocket.ts). Move all state to module-level. Remove onUnmounted auto-cleanup. Add setOnData() method to update the data callback after construction. Capture must survive route navigation FlowLive→FlowWaiting→FlowStreaming.

sub_plan.description: Convert useAudioCapture from per-instance to singleton composable

steps.task: Move all refs (devices, selectedDeviceId, isCapturing, isRecording, error, inputVolume, mediaStream, processedStream) and private vars (mediaRecorder, audioContext, gainNode, sourceNode, destinationNode) to module-level scope, outside the useAudioCapture() function. Keep function as the public API surface.

Remove the onUnmounted(() => stopCapture()) hook. Add a setOnData(callback) method that updates the onData callback at runtime. This allows FlowWaiting to wire onData → streamSocket.send() without re-creating the composable.

knowledge.notes: Critical: StreamPage.vue passes onData via constructor options. The new setOnData() method lets FlowWaiting set it later since the singleton is created before the stream socket exists.

steps.task: Update all consumers of useAudioCapture: FlowLive.vue (remove reliance on onUnmounted cleanup), FlowWaiting.vue (use singleton instance, wire data via setOnData), FlowStreaming.vue (use singleton for meter/volume), StreamPage.vue (verify still works with setOnData in constructor).

decisions: Singleton pattern chosen to match useStreamSocket — audio capture must persist across FlowLive→FlowWaiting→FlowStreaming route changes
setOnData() method over constructor option — the data sink (streamSocket.send) doesn't exist when useAudioCapture is first called in FlowLive

steps.task: Fix FlowWaiting.vue handleGoLive(): use singleton useAudioCapture with setOnData(data => streamSocket.send(data)), then call audioCapture.startRecording() after socket connects. Remove manual MediaRecorder creation. This restores the StreamPage.vue pattern from commit 07f39e4.

decisions: Restore onData→send wiring pattern from StreamPage.vue L25-L34 instead of manual MediaRecorder creation

steps.task: Fix public listener site: add polling to main.ts (check stream status every 8s), add player reconnection logic to player.ts (destroy and re-create FLV player on live transitions), fix CSP in index.html to allow HLS segment fetches.

sub_plan.description: Public site stream detection polling and player reconnection

steps.task: Update main.ts: replace single checkStreamStatus() call with setInterval polling every 8 seconds. Track previous state to detect live→offline and offline→live transitions. On transition to live: call updateLiveStatus(true) and restartPlayer(). On transition to offline: call updateLiveStatus(false) and destroyPlayer().

knowledge.notes: 8s interval balances responsiveness with server load. HEAD request is lightweight.

steps.task: Update player.ts: export destroyPlayer() and restartPlayer() functions. destroyPlayer() cleans up existing FLV player or HLS audio. restartPlayer() creates a fresh player instance. FLV player must be fully destroyed and re-created on each offline→live transition to avoid stale state.

references: source/frontend/src/player.ts L26-L44 (current FLV player init, no reconnect logic)

steps.task: Fix CSP in index.html: broaden connect-src to include 'https://stream.moafunk.de' (wildcard for HLS .ts segment fetches and .m3u8) instead of just the exact .m3u8 and .flv URLs.

decisions: Polling over SSE/WebSocket for public site — simpler, HEAD requests are cheap, no backend changes needed
Full player destroy+re-create on transitions — FLV.js has stale buffer issues when attempting to reconnect

steps.task: Fix FlowStreaming.vue upload-mode status polling: change fetch('/api/stream-status') to use streamApi.status() (correct URL /api/stream/status), change data.is_live to data.active to match backend StreamStatus struct.

decisions: Use streamApi.status() from api/index.ts rather than raw fetch — already correctly targets /api/stream/status and returns typed response

steps.task: Add recordStream ref to useHostFlow.ts composable. Export recordStream and setRecordStream(val) action. Default false. Persists across FlowWaiting→FlowStreaming navigation.

Add 'Record this show' checkbox to FlowWaiting.vue. Bind to flow.recordStream. When handleGoLive() fires and recordStream is true, call POST /api/recording/start with show ID (using existing recordingApi) to start server-side recording tee after stream socket connects.

Add recording indicator to FlowStreaming.vue: show red REC dot when backend reports recording=true via status polling. For live mode, add toggle button to start/stop recording mid-stream via POST /api/recording/start and /api/recording/stop. Import streamApi for status checks.
Update FlowStreaming.vue onUnmounted: if recording is active, call POST /api/recording/stop. Ensure audioCapture.stopCapture() and streamSocket.stopStream() are called explicitly (singleton cleanup).
Frontend build verification: run npm run build + npm run test in source/frontend/. Fix any TypeScript errors, import issues, or test failures.
Update streamDetector.test.ts if needed to cover new polling behavior. Verify existing tests pass with singleton useAudioCapture changes.
